output.subject: We have received your complaint about the Zelle payment of 16 September
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for writing to us. We have received your complaint, and we're sorry for the distress this situation has caused you.

You told us that on 16 September you received a text message that appeared to come from us, saying someone was using your account. You mentioned that a man then called you, that your screen showed "Meridian Harbor Bank," and that he told you to protect your money by sending it to yourself through Zelle. You said you sent $2,450 to a number he described as a secure account, and that he turned out to be a scammer.

You also told us that when you called us the same day, you were told nothing could be done because you had "authorized" the payment. You said you did not authorize a thief, and that because your English is not very strong, you did not fully understand what was explained to you on the phone. You have asked for our help in recovering your $2,450.

A specialist team is reviewing your complaint and will respond within 10 business days.

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: The customer wrote in Spanish and says limited English kept them from understanding the bank's phone explanation.
This reply is in English so the approver can read every word; arrange a Spanish translation of the approved text, including the subject line, before it is sent.
The reply makes no promise of interpreter services, Spanish-speaking staff or callbacks; add any such offer only if you confirm it is available.
The customer says they were told on the day of the call that nothing could be done; confirm what was said and whether a fraud claim was actually opened.
The customer is asking to recover $2,450. The reply makes no commitment on recovery, so the specialist team must decide the outcome.
The complaint includes the recipient phone number; it is left out of the reply and should be checked in the case record, not the letter.
